See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Question minutes = (Exam minutes − Review minutes) ÷ Total marks × Question marks

A worked example

A 120-minute exam with 15 minutes reserved leaves 105 working minutes. With 100 marks available, that is 1.05 minutes per mark. A 12-mark question receives 12.6 minutes in this proportional plan.

Before you use the result

This is a time budget based on marks, not a rule that every mark takes the same effort. Question marks cannot exceed the exam total and the checking reserve must leave positive working time. Use the marks for the questions you must answer, accounting for optional sections and the actual exam instructions.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Should I include marks for optional questions I will not attempt?

No. Use the total marks for the set of questions required to complete your paper.

What if essay and short-answer questions need different pacing?

Use this as an initial budget, then adapt it to the demands of each section and your practice-paper experience.
